topics.title: Rolle's Theorem
topics.sourceText: If f(x) is continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and f(a) = f(b), then there exists at least one c in (a,b) such that f'(c) = 0. A smooth curve that returns to the same height must have a horizontal tangent somewhere in between.

mapping.Connection / Reason: The song's theme of ending up back where you started mirrors f(a) = f(b), with a flat tangent guaranteed somewhere in between.

topics.title: Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem
topics.sourceText: If f(x) is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), there exists c in (a,b) such that f'(c) = [f(b) - f(a)] / (b - a). It generalizes Rolle's theorem by relating average rate of change to an instantaneous rate at an interior point.

mapping.Connection / Reason: The theorem guarantees a point 'in the middle' where the instantaneous rate matches the average rate over the whole interval.

topics.title: Cauchy's Mean Value Theorem
topics.sourceText: If f(x) and g(x) are continuous on [a,b], differentiable on (a,b), and g'(x) != 0 on (a,b), there exists c in (a,b) such that [f(b)-f(a)] / [g(b)-g(a)] = f'(c) / g'(c). It is the ratio form of Lagrange's theorem for two functions.

mapping.Chapter: Differential Calculus of Functions of One Variable
mapping.Artist: Bill Withers, Grover Washington Jr. & Ralph MacDonald
mapping.Connection / Reason: Two functions f and g are compared side by side as a ratio, generalising the single-function idea of Lagrange's theorem.

topics.title: Convergence of Sequences
topics.sourceText: A sequence {a_n} converges to a limit L if for every epsilon > 0 there exists N such that |a_n - L| < epsilon for all n > N. Monotone bounded sequences are a key sufficient condition for convergence.

topics.title: Convergence of Series
topics.sourceText: An infinite series sum(a_n) converges if its sequence of partial sums S_n = a_1 + a_2 + ... + a_n tends to a finite limit. Standard tests include comparison test, ratio (D'Alembert's) test, root (Cauchy's) test, and integral test.

topics.title: L'Hospital's Rule
topics.sourceText: If lim[x->a] f(x)/g(x) gives 0/0 or infinity/infinity, then lim[x->a] f(x)/g(x) = lim[x->a] f'(x)/g'(x), provided the latter limit exists; the rule can be applied repeatedly for higher-order indeterminate forms.

mapping.Connection / Reason: The rule 'fixes' an indeterminate form by swapping it for the ratio of derivatives, resolving what direct substitution can't.

topics.title: Limits and Continuity of Functions of Several Variables

topics.title: Partial Differentiation
topics.sourceText: For f(x,y), partial f/partial x differentiates with respect to x while holding y constant, and partial f/partial y differentiates with respect to y while holding x constant. Higher-order partials include partial^2f/partial x^2, partial^2f/partial y^2, and the mixed partial partial^2f/(partial x partial y).

topics.title: Maxima and Minima of Functions of Two Variables
topics.sourceText: Stationary points occur where f_x = 0 and f_y = 0. With r = f_xx, s = f_xy, t = f_yy at that point: rt - s^2 > 0 and r < 0 gives a maximum; rt - s^2 > 0 and r > 0 gives a minimum; rt - s^2 < 0 gives a saddle point; rt - s^2 = 0 is inconclusive.

topics.title: Gradient
topics.sourceText: For a scalar field phi(x,y,z), grad(phi) = del(phi) = (partial phi/partial x)i + (partial phi/partial y)j + (partial phi/partial z)k is a vector pointing in the direction of steepest increase of phi, with magnitude equal to the maximum rate of increase.

topics.title: Divergence

topics.title: Curl

topics.title: Scalar Potential

topics.title: Green's Theorem
topics.sourceText: Integral-over-C (P dx + Q dy) = Integral-over-R (partial Q/partial x - partial P/partial y) dA, relating a line integral around simple closed curve C to a double integral over the plane region R it encloses.

topics.title: Stokes' Theorem
topics.sourceText: Integral-over-C F . dr = Integral-over-S (curl F) . n-hat dS, relating a line integral around closed curve C to a surface integral of curl(F) over any surface S bounded by C; generalizes Green's theorem to three dimensions.

topics.title: Gauss Divergence Theorem
